note.text: Air transport can serve urgent, light or high-value flows but needs airports, suitable aircraft and connecting services. Water transport can suit large non-urgent freight flows where ports and navigable routes exist, but terminal handling and onward movement matter. Neither is always cheapest or fastest for every complete journey. Cargo needs, connections and reliability determine an appropriate choice.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to choose a mode for a stated cargo and explain the trade-off. Builds on: road and rail impacts. Leads to: specialised transport and pipelines.

sections.heading: Explain the geography
sections.text: Air transport can serve urgent, light or high-value flows but needs airports, suitable aircraft and connecting services. Water transport can suit large non-urgent freight flows where ports and navigable routes exist, but terminal handling and onward movement matter. Neither is always cheapest or fastest for every complete journey. Cargo needs, connections and reliability determine an appropriate choice.

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: In fictional offers, urgent small documents can take an available air service, while non-urgent bulk machinery can use an available sea route between ports. A village away from either terminal still needs a connecting movement. These classroom offers are not live schedules, fares or navigation instructions.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Read urgency, size, route availability and delivery destination. Compare the whole chain, including transfer and final access. Justify the chosen mode using the stated conditions rather than a universal slogan about speed or cost.

pick.q: Invented offers: urgent small documents must arrive tomorrow; an air service meets that deadline and the offered sea service does not. Which fits?
w: The offered sea service
No transport because a message was sent
Any mode regardless of deadline
e: The stated sea offer misses the deadline.
Physical documents still need movement.
The deadline is a selection condition.
pick.y: Use the actual offers, not an unconditional claim about all aircraft.

A telephone call carrying the cargo
A railway absent from the offered routes
e: The air offer fails the stated budget.
Calls transmit information, not this cargo.
An unavailable route cannot be chosen.
pick.y: Select a feasible offer that meets cargo and budget conditions.

Ships use suitable water routes.
